children: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD, Financials), is taking a breather after one of its strongest stretches of the year, with shares falling 1.5% Wednesday to $614.10 after six consecutive sessions of gains.
The pullback was modest compared with the recent rally. AMD climbed roughly 24% during those six sessions and is now up more than 180% this year, far ahead of the broader S&P 500's roughly 13% gain.
The stock also recently crossed the $1 trillion market-cap threshold for the first time, joining Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron among chipmakers at that level.
AMD's September run has been particularly strong. The stock finished higher in 10 of the month's first 15 sessions and is up nearly 35% over the past month.

The bigger story is still AI. Investors are betting AMD can continue gaining ground in data-center GPUs as demand for AI computing expands. Seeking Alpha analyst Andres Veurink said he sees a path to substantially higher revenue if AMD captures a larger share of the data-center GPU market.
At the same time, AMD is trading at about 81 times forward earnings, according to Seeking Alpha data, putting more attention on how quickly earnings can catch up with the stock's gains.
The next catalyst is AMD's upcoming financial results, which should provide a clearer look at whether its AI-driven growth is keeping pace with the market's higher expectations.

title: AMD's Six-Day Rally Finally Hits a Pause
